title: Explain the human role when working with agents
lead: Explain what a human decides and observes when using agents with slicer, from agreeing on the work through reviewing evidence and deciding whether to integrate it.
findings_note: Owner documentation review 2026-10-16; docs/agents.md is an agent/JSON reference and docs/tui.md describes controls, but neither is a human operator's end-to-end guide. Existing s331 addresses finished-run status presentation; s319, s320, s322 and s332 address relay contracts, roles, briefs and recording rather than this documentation gap.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** implementing queued relay or TUI features, a new agent harness, changing relay contracts or role matrices, duplicating vendor/model tables, or automating owner decisions.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: AI contracts describe agent obligations, but the owner also needs to understand their own responsibilities, how to inspect work, and what remains after a run reports success. In particular, a relay gate passing does not establish that a slice is merged or marked done.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- Create docs/working-with-agents.md.
- Link it from README.md, docs/getting-started.md, and docs/agents.md.
- Consult slicer ai relay, slicer ai relay-orchestrator, relay-roles help/recommendations, docs/tui.md, and existing command documentation when describing the current workflow.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body: No tests asserting prose wording are required. Validate each inspection recipe against shipped command help and available read-only behavior; do not launch paid agents or create external side effects as a documentation check.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Cover agreeing on goals and constraints; reviewing evidence-based findings against the existing roadmap; approving bounded specifications and acceptance checks; selecting manual implementation, one agent, or a relay; confirming relay roles and the endpoint; supervising progress; reviewing checks and handoff evidence; and explicitly deciding when to integrate work.

Include a Mermaid sequence diagram distinguishing owner, outer session, orchestrator, implementer, and reviewer/gate. Explain optional architecture review according to the live relay contract and show the reject/fix/review loop without copying the contract text. Explain that slicer stores and reports work rather than launching AI services.

Provide short recipes using shipped status, show, log, relay-run list, and the TUI relay board. Explain what each surface can establish and how to identify work waiting on a human decision. Distinguish run outcome, review/handoff status, branch integration, and slice completion. Explain that board visibility depends on recorded events rather than implying full process control.

Link to generated agent instructions and relay contracts as authoritative, and to relay-roles recommendations instead of copying model choices. Link back to this human guide from the agent reference so both audiences can find the division of responsibilities. Describe commands as shipped at implementation time; queued s319/s320/s322/s327/s331/s332 behavior is not a prerequisite and must not be presented as already available.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- A reader can name their decisions, inspect an active run using documented surfaces, understand a failed review or handoff, and identify what remains before completion.
- Review the sequence against the live relay contract and configured finish policy; verify links and anchors.
- Check command examples against help and existing local read-only data. Do not launch agents, commit, merge, or publish as a walkthrough check.
- Render the guide with quire --config squalor to ignored .venv/docs-preview/ and visually inspect labels, clipping, and page breaks; retain prose explanations for readers without Mermaid rendering. Record any rendering blocker.
- Run affected tests, slicer check, and git diff --check; follow the full-suite requirement if source or tests change.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Use a fresh slice worktree. Review documentation, tracking, and generated output together. Finish with the required note and handoff after acceptance passes. Commit only when authorized; owner integration and publication decisions remain separate.
